contentEn:
Reno Stars has been finishing Coquitlam basements since 2015. A new secondary suite in Coquitlam costs $38,000–$95,000+, depending on suite size, condition, and permit requirements. An existing unfinished basement renovation runs $22,000–$55,000. This guide covers BC legalization rules, current 2026 permit costs, and real project budgets from Coquitlam homeowners.

How Much Does a Basement Suite Renovation Cost in Coquitlam in 2026?

Coquitlam basement suite costs depend on whether you are converting an unfinished space or building a new suite from scratch.

ScopeCost Range
New secondary suite (from unfinished basement)$38,000 – $95,000+
Existing suite renovation / upgrade$22,000 – $55,000
Building permit (Coquitlam)$1,500 – $4,000
Electrical permit + inspection$800 – $2,000
Plumbing permit$600 – $1,500
radon testing + energy audit$400 – $800

Coquitlam charges $2,500–$8,000 in municipal fees for secondary suite legalization, on top of the building permit. Budget an additional $3,000–$6,000 for architectural or engineering drawings if your home is post-1990.

Reno Stars provides itemized quotes for Coquitlam homeowners — get a free estimate for your specific project.

What Permits Does a Coquitlam Basement Suite Need?

Coquitlam basement suites are regulated under the BC Secondary Suite Authorization Act and Coquitlam's zoning bylaw. All suites require:

  • Building permit (structural, fire separation, ceiling height)
  • Electrical permit + ESA inspection
  • Plumbing permit + inspection
  • Radon testing (mandatory since 2023)
  • Energy efficiency audit (EnerGuide assessment)
  • BC Housing compliance inspection (for rental suites)

Coquitlam's Planning Department processes secondary suite applications within 4–8 weeks after a complete submission. Reno Stars handles the full permit application process for Coquitlam homeowners.

How Long Does a Coquitlam Basement Suite Renovation Take?

A typical Coquitlam basement suite renovation takes 3–6 months from permit application to final inspection:

  • Permit application + approval: 4–8 weeks
  • Demolition + rough-in: 2–4 weeks
  • Framing, insulation, drywall: 2–3 weeks
  • Electrical + plumbing: 1–2 weeks
  • Finishing + fixtures: 2–3 weeks
  • Final inspections: 1–2 weeks

BC's Suite Registration Act means Coquitlam homeowners can rent suites legally once all inspections pass — no need to remove the suite if it meets code.

What Is the BC Secondary Suite Financing Program?

Eligible BC homeowners can access CMHC Canadian Priority Block Financing — up to $60,000 in federal loans at prime rate, specifically for secondary suite conversions. Funds cover foundation, electrical, plumbing, and fire safety upgrades.

The RDH Rebate offers additional provincial grants for homeowners meeting income thresholds. Reno Stars helps Coquitlam clients navigate financing options during the quote process.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I add a basement suite to my Coquitlam home?

Yes, if your property meets BC Secondary Suite Authorization Act requirements and Coquitlam zoning bylaw: adequate lot size, parking, ceiling height (minimum 2.13 m / 7 ft), and fire separation standards. Reno Stars reviews your property specifics before quoting.

Does a basement suite increase property value in Coquitlam?

Yes. A legal secondary suite typically adds $75,000–$150,000 to Coquitlam assessed value, depending on suite size and finish quality. Monthly rental income also helps offset mortgage costs.

What is the minimum size for a legal basement suite in BC?

BC requires a secondary suite's floor area to be at least 32 m² (344 ft²) and no more than 90 m² (969 ft²), or 40% of the home's total floor area — whichever is less.

Does Coquitlam allow basement suites in all zones?

No. Coquitlam permits secondary suites in most RS1–RS7 single-family zones, but not in estate zones or areas with specific geological constraints. Your Reno Stars quote includes a zoning check for your address.
